text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Swiss Defence Minister Adolf Ogi flew to Sarajevo on Tuesday to talk to representatives of multinational Bosnian Troops and to visit Swiss peacekeeping troops.
- Swiss Interior Minister Ruth Dreifuss said at a Geneva memorial service for Jewish victims of the Holocaust Monday that Switzerland still has debts to pay regarding the past.
- Aare-Tessin AG for Electricity (ATEL) reported a group profit increase of 3.7 percent to a record high of 167 million Swiss francs for 1996.

- Swiss National Bank shares doubled in price on the Swiss stock exchange within three days for no apparent reason. The Canton of Zurich, a majority shareholder, had a paper gain of seven million francs due to the rise.
- Zurich Cantonal Bank reported a 20.1 percent rise in gross profit to 154.7 million Swiss francs for the first quarter of 1997, compared to the same period last year.
- Nestle food group posted a first quarter sales increase of 18.7 percent to 16.1 billion Swiss francs.
- Logitech International S.A. registered a 157 percent profit rise to $21.06 million for the 1996/97 fiscal year ended March 31.
- Peter Brabeck will become CEO of Nestle starting June 5, when Helmut Maucher steps down after having run the company for years in a period when performance was very strong.
